Wings at War
tags: Nature, Elementals, Angels and demons, Farm, Craft, Monster Report, Achievements, Manage items, inspired by Ragnarok Online and Skyrim
​
Spoiler:
What is Wings at War?
A hybrid pixel art RPG with elements of visual novel, crafting, and puzzles, set in an epic post-deluge world. It blends RPG Maker XP-style graphics with high-resolution visual effects (such as lighting and anime-style illustrations), creating a unique aesthetic that bridges the nostalgic and the cinematic. The player explores ancient ruins, activates technological artifacts mistaken for magic, and interacts with various races like elves, goblins, fairies, demons, and angels. The narrative is deep, filled with choices, combat, and personal progression — the hero shapes himself through his actions, in the midst of an ancient mythology on the verge of awakening.
​
Spoiler:
Synopsis
The game consists in episodes, the first episode is free.
The story puts the player character into a group known as The Flag Bearers. This group was created by the humans after they discovered an ancient artifact with magical properties. Through the supervision of the government, selected and approved members of the Flag Bearers can make a pact with the magical artifact, giving them some form of enhancement in exchange for a binding sacrifice. There are two variants of this pact. The first is the one the player-character is bound to, the Red Wing. The Red Wing Pact binds the pact maker to a life of servitude as an aether collector. The Black Wing Pact binds the pact maker to a commitment of management in a community. Whether that be familially, politically, or commercially. The “winged” name of the pact stems from those who have a long experience over time with the pact, hearing a distinct magical voice and fluttering of wings.As stated before, the pact with the red wing and the black wing has its advantages and disadvantages...The Red Wing Pact grants the user enhanced combat and speed skills.The Black Wing Pact grants the user an extended life span.One crucial fact of these pacts is that they cannot be broken. If a pact-maker fails in their bound duties they will gradually begin to succumb to a deadly illness. The only way to recover from this ailment is returning to one's duties.
​
Spoiler:
LORE
Wings at War – Base Lore
The Current World
“Before Aetherya there was another world. One brimming with wonder and change. Some say this was the world of magic. Other say the Gods. The only thing for certain is that world is now gone, buried by The Great Flood.” - An exerpt from “The Origins of Artherya” by an unknown author.
Aetherya is but one planet that sits amongst a sea of many constellations and planets. Within this plane of reality, Aetherya acts as our anchor. Within Aetherya lies 12 continents, most filled with mystery and intrigue. These landmasses are separated by vast oceans containing terrifying creatures and horrible waves.
Aether is a mysterious floating fluid that strengthens magical barriers, it is widely used by all creatures to strengthen the protection of their cities. Some creatures even feed on it, but why, how and where they appear is a mystery. Being found randomly throughout the world.
Our story begins on Delkaria. Delkaria is a land of various climates, cultures, and biomes. From the harsh winter and cold winds of Bravholt to the smooth hot sands of Ostara. From the field of vibrant grass in Aldebron even to the magical awe of the floating city of Sylveria, Delkaria is a land of wonder.
Aldebron, Bravholt, Sylveria, Ostara, and Nevalis make up the five human civilizations of Delkaria under the Delkar Republic. Heraalded by one great leader, each civilization is run by govenors.
While humans are the main inhabitors of Delkaria, within this country there are other ceatures and beings who live there as well. Goblins and Elementals are just a few of the other civilizations scattered throughout the region.
The world where Wings at War takes place is the result of a cataclysm known only as The Flood. It is uncertain whether this was a natural disaster, a magical event, or a divine punishment. What humans do know is that everything that existed before was swallowed — cities, technologies, civilizations, planets, stars… Everything disappeared.
The continent inhabited by humans today is just a small fraction of what is believed to be the world. They live isolated, surrounded by dangerous oceans inhabited by colossal magical creatures that make navigation impossible.
This new world is populated not only by humans but also by beings they call “monsters”: elementals, goblins, ogres, chimeras, and even more enigmatic entities such as angels and demons. However, these creatures are not simple beasts — they are descendants, or direct creations, of an era before the Flood.
The Lost Truth (Hidden Knowledge)
In the hidden truth of the creators, this world is a distorted reflection of an alternate future of our own Earth, where humanity mastered genetics, AI, and even virtual realities to the point where the boundaries between the natural and the created were erased.
Humans modified their own DNA.
They created new species from animals, artificial intelligence, and genetic manipulation.
They created hyper-realistic games, and even simulated realities that became as complex as physical reality.
The Flood was, in fact, the collapse of this entire hyperstructure — a total reset of civilization. But this is unknown to current humans. Only fragments remain: legends, technological ruins mistaken for magic, and the pre-Flood beings now known as the Heralds. These Heralds hold mysterious secrets that shine a light on the world before The Great Flood.
Political and Social System
Humans: They are the minority. They live in a Republic, governed by an elected President and assisted by governors, mayors, and counselors. Each city has a governor.
Angels and Demons: They live in monarchies or theocracies, based on bloodlines or mystical hierarchies.
Other races: Organized into tribes, clans, councils, or simply orbiting their own Heralds, who are like semi-divine figures.
Heralds – The Pre-Flood Entities
Each race has a Herald, a being that survived the Flood and carries part of the Truth of Creation.
They are the cultural founders of the races.
Not all Heralds are active. Some have disappeared.
The Herald of humanity is missing, creating a great philosophical, spiritual, and even political void.
Examples:
Herald of the Goblins: A creature half goblin, half something else, marked with ancestral power, who taught goblins their culture, writing, and rituals.
Herald of the Elementals: Each element has a single Herald, being almost like forces of nature itself.
Herald of the Angels: A living archetype of purity and wisdom, but distant and practically inaccessible.
Religion and Beliefs
There is no consensus on deities.
Each people worships their Herald as if they were a god, but some believe in a single god or in multiple gods.
The concept of God, or gods, is an absolute mystery and will never be clearly answered, reinforcing the philosophical tone of the game.
The Central Conflict
The war between the desire to dominate reality and the forces that fight to preserve the mysteries of creation.
Explanation:
After centuries struggling to survive, humanity has begun to rediscover the secrets of magic — which is nothing more than a degenerated form of ancient technology and reality manipulation.
The problem: tampering with the structure of creation has consequences. The very laws of reality begin to distort.
This brings forth creatures, forces, dormant heralds, and even disturbances in existence itself.
Other races, such as angels, demons, and elementals, watch humanity with suspicion.
Some wish to protect the balance. Others seek to exploit the chaos.
Thus, the war begins not only against external enemies but against the very nature of reality and human ambition.
World Name:
Aetherya (Aether + Earth)
Continents:
12 continents — the starting continent for players is called:
Delkaria
The Human Republic:
Delkar
“Long ago, our ancestors witnessed the fury of the Flood. A catastrophe so vast that it erased not only our cities but also the very memory of what we once were. From the wreckage of reality, we rose, building the Republic of Delkar.
We know we are not alone. Strange creatures roam the world — some intelligent, others beastly. Goblins, ogres, elementals, and even legends of Angels and Demons, beings said to be as old as creation itself.
But who are we? Where did we come from?
All we know is that magic permeates everything. Our scholars claim it is a gift, a tool. Others whisper it is a curse — a remnant of an age we should never have rediscovered.
And as we seek understanding… something watches us. Perhaps the gods. Perhaps the Heralds. Perhaps something far worse.”
World: Aetherya
Meaning: “Ethereal Earth” or “Land of the Veils” — a world where the fabric between planes (physical, spiritual, elemental, and astral) is thinner, allowing the emergence of magic, entities, and supernatural phenomena.
Starting Continent: Delkaria
A region marked by great contrasts: from magical forests and trade deserts to icy mountains and cursed ruins.
Home to the main human nation: The Republic of Delkar, founded after the flood.
Aldebron — The City of Light
Role in the world: Capital of the Republic of Delkar. The political, spiritual, and cultural center of humans.
Connections:
Maintains magical and diplomatic treaties with Sylveria (mages) and trade agreements with Ostara.
Bravholt — The Northern Fortress
Role in the world: Military stronghold of the Republic, protecting the north of Delkaria
Connections:
Supplies warriors and runic artifacts to Aldebron and Ostara.
Sends battle mages to Sylveria for studies creatures.
Sylveria — The City of Mages
Role in the world: Guardian of magical secrets.
Connections:
Collaborates with Aldebron to maintain spiritual balance.
Trades magical artifacts with Ostara.
Ostara — The Merchant’s Village
Role in the world: The economic heart of Delkaria, neutral in political and military matters, but essential to all.
Connections:
The only city that maintains trade (legal or illegal) with explorers from Nevalis.
Hosts secret markets of forbidden artifacts
Serves as a bridge for information and goods between Aldebron, Bravholt, and Sylveria.
Nevalis — The Lost City
Role in the world: The epicenter of Collapse 400 years ago. Its study is vital to understanding the risks of magical imbalance.
Connections:
Explorers from all other cities try to plunder or study its mysteries.
Nevalis is an open wound in the world — its unstable portals sometimes connect to random locations, creating anomalies in Delkaria.
How These Cities Sustain the Global Lore:
Aldebron: Spiritual and religious defense.
Bravholt: Physical and military defense.
Sylveria: Arcane and mystical defense.
Ostara: Connections, resources, and information.
Nevalis: The origin of the problem — and possibly the solution.
The story follows a person who is part of the group called Flag Bearers. This group was created by the humans after they discovered a magical artifact and approved by the government. The selected and approved members of this group make a pact with the magical artifact, the pact is called Red Wing for those who commit to living a life as Aether collectors and Black Wing for those who commit to managing for the collective good everything from family, commercial ventures to government. It has this name because those successful and advanced in the pact say they can hear a winged being.
but the pact with the red wing and the black wing has its advantages and disadvantages...
The pact with red wing gives combat and locomotion skills.
The pact with black wings gives extended life span.
The pact cannot be broken, but if the person begins to fail to comply with what was agreed upon, he will gradually begin to get sick until he dies or returns to what was agreed upon in the pact and recovers his health.
